/-!
# Erdős Problem 1096

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1096](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1096)
- [ErKo98] Erdős, P. and Komornik, V., Developments in non-integer bases.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1998), 57--83.
- [Fe16] Feng, D.-J., On the topology of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients.
  J. Eur. Math. Soc. (2016), 181--193.
-/

open Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1096

/--
Let $1<q<1+\epsilon$ and consider the set of numbers of the shape
$\sum_{i\in S}q^i$ (for all finite $S$), ordered by size as
$0=x_1<x_2<\cdots$.

Is it true that, provided $\epsilon>0$ is sufficiently small, $x_{k+1}-x_k \to 0$?

This was solved affirmatively by Erdős and Komornik [ErKo98], who proved the conclusion
whenever $1<q<\sqrt{q_1}$, where $q_1$ is the second Pisot-Vijayaraghavan number.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1096.lean#L44"]
theorem erdos_1096 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ ε > 0, ∀ q, 1 < q → q < 1 + ε →
    ∀ x : ℕ → ℝ, StrictMono x → Set.range x = { ∑ i ∈ S, q ^ i | S : Finset ℕ } →
    Tendsto (fun k => x (k + 1) - x k) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: add variants and additional material from the Erdős Problems page.

end Erdos1096

reformulations.difference: Instead of fixing the source's ordered sequence 0 = x₁ < x₂ < ⋯, Lean universally quantifies over strictly increasing ℕ-indexed sequences having exactly the finite-sum set as their range. It does not explicitly require x 0 = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every q > 1, the finite-sum set has a unique increasing enumeration. Indeed, choose N with B < q^N: any sum at most B uses only exponents below N, so there are finitely many such values. The set is unbounded because it contains every q^n, and its least element is 0, supplied by the empty sum. Thus the enumeration hypotheses are satisfiable, determine a unique sequence, and imply x 0 = 0. In /workspace/review/enumeration.lean, I proved existence, uniqueness, the initial-value property, and an equivalence between the universal formulation and existence of an enumeration starting at zero with any prescribed property. I also proved invariance of the gap limit under the initial index shift.
